do_more: Use authoritative, classic titles (e.g., "The Principles Of Psychology") without emojis or click‑bait symbols
Keep videos tight – aim for ~30 seconds to maintain high average watch %
Create a consistent series tag like "Reading X" to build repeat viewers
Focus on single, concrete concepts from public‑domain texts and present them as a clear takeaway
Add a brief on‑screen citation of the original author to boost credibility
avoid: Overly sensational hook phrases or emojis in the title
Very broad or vague topics that lack a clear, single lesson
Longer runtimes (>45 seconds) that drop average watch %
short.title_style: Straightforward, scholarly phrasing – "The [Concept] Explained – [Classic Book/Author]" with no emojis
next_tests: Release two 30‑second shorts on different classic works and compare VPD to a 45‑second version of the same topic
Add a "Reading X" series label to half of new videos and leave the others unlabeled to see impact on repeat views
Swap a click‑bait title for a scholarly title on a low‑performing video and track changes in VPD

do_more: Pick concrete, observable topics (behavior, efficiency, emotion) instead of abstract concepts
Begin titles with a clear subject, a colon, then a specific hook (e.g., "Psychology: Why Workplace Efficiency Fails – Guided Reading")
Deliver the main hook within the first 30 seconds to grab attention
Label the format consistently (e.g., "Guided reading" or "Reading X") after the main title
Target a standard segment length of about 42 seconds for each reading segment
avoid: Vague, broad titles like "The Psychology Of Revolution"
Opening with generic phrases such as "How We Think" without a concrete angle
Relying on high watch‑time percentages without improving click‑through appeal
full.title_style: Use a concrete subject, add a colon, then a specific, curiosity‑driving hook followed by the format tag
next_tests: A/B test titles with colon‑style hooks vs plain titles to measure VPD
Create two video cuts: one with a ~30‑second tight hook and one with a ~42‑second standard hook to see which drives more views
Add a brief "Did you know?" fact at the start of the video and compare click‑through rates
